rows.title: Lamont to cancel tax relief, seek labor savings to shrink $2B deficit in July
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont said he would cancel tax relief and seek labor savings to mitigate a big deficit in July.

rows.title: Some CT businesses, but not all, receiving stimulus loans in second round this week
rows.standfirst: Some firms have been granted loans in this week’s round of distributions. Others are still waiting.

rows.title: CT can delay its transportation financing debate only a few months more
rows.standfirst: With revenues evaporating and upgrades long overdue, Connecticut will have to act soon to solve its transportation financing problems.

rows.title: CT receives 38,000 unemployment claims from self-employed and ‘gig’ workers, but benefit payments will take a while longer
rows.standfirst: There is still an additional process for these workers to receive federal benefits under the CARES Act.

rows.title: Nonprofits: Lamont has not delivered promised PPE
rows.standfirst: Nonprofit social service agencies accused Gov. Ned Lamont with failing to deliver protective gear pledged two weeks ago.

rows.title: Latinos have nation’s highest unemployment rate, and in Connecticut it could be extreme
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus pandemic has ravaged sectors of the economy where Latinos and other people of color are likely to work.

rows.title: CT struggling to detail coronavirus’ impact on assisted living centers
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s efforts to track the coronavirus in assisted living centers continues to have significant gaps after two weeks.

rows.title: House Dems propose new $1,200 stimulus checks, billions for states, renters, and essential workers
rows.standfirst: Connecticut Democrats support the $3 trillion bill, but Republicans say the ‘wish list’ is DOA.

rows.title: In new stimulus bill, Pelosi rejects Blumenthal-sponsored paycheck guarantee proposal
rows.standfirst: House progressives want to hold up the vote for the HEROES Act, in part because the paycheck provision isn’t included.

rows.title: Auditors: CT continues to pay millions of $ in pension benefits above legal limits
rows.standfirst: Connecticut continues to pay millions of dollars annually in pension benefits beyond federal and contractual limits, state auditors reported Monday.

rows.title: Ready to gamble? Mohegan Sun wants to take your temperature.
rows.standfirst: The Mohegans want the governor’s blessing to reopen the casino. He’s not ready to give it.

rows.title: Progressives look to bring CT’s tax fairness debate to the grassroots level
rows.standfirst: The next Connecticut income tax debate is heating up — but not at the Capitol.

rows.title: Lamont hopes the friendly approach will coax unions to the table
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont is hoping a friendly approach will entice state employees to sacrifice yet another pay raise.

rows.title: CT suffers April job losses of ‘epic proportions’ with 266,000 positions gone
rows.standfirst: The effective unemployment rate is around 17.5%, the labor commissioner says.

rows.title: CCM chastises Lamont for not sharing federal relief funds with cities and towns
rows.standfirst: The Connecticut Conference of Municipalities chastised Gov. Ned Lamont Thursday for not sending emerrgency federal pandemic funding directly to communities.

rows.title: Federal Bank predicts a Connecticut surge of pandemic-induced missed rent and mortgage payments
rows.standfirst: The Boston Fed predicts 11% percent of Connecticut homeowners and 36% of state renters could miss payments.

rows.title: CT heads to Wall Street to jump-start its construction industry
rows.standfirst: Connecticut is taking a big step toward re-energizing its construction economy, seeking nearly $1.4 billion in financing.
